title: Two particles on a line: direction and speed

stimulus.title: Positions of two particles
stimulus.text: Particles $P$ and $Q$ move along the $x$-axis for $0 \le t \le 6$. Their positions are given below, with $x$ in meters and $t$ in seconds.

table.caption: Positions of particles P and Q at time t seconds, in meters

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the velocity of particle $P$ at time $t = 2$. Is $P$ moving to the left or to the right at $t = 2$? Give a reason for your answer.

accept: the reason must be the sign of the velocity

parts.sample: $v_P(t) = x_P'(t) = 6t^2 - 30t + 24$, so $v_P(2) = 24 - 60 + 24 = -12$ meters per second. Since $v_P(2) < 0$, particle $P$ is moving to the left at $t = 2$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Is particle $P$ speeding up or slowing down at time $t = 2$? Give a reason for your answer.

rubric.point: Speeding up, because $v_P(2)$ and $a_P(2)$ are both negative
accept: both signs must be named; "$a < 0$" alone does not earn the point

parts.sample: $a_P(t) = v_P'(t) = 12t - 30$, so $a_P(2) = -6$. Since $v_P(2) = -12 < 0$ and $a_P(2) = -6 < 0$ have the same sign, particle $P$ is speeding up at $t = 2$.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find all times $t$, for $0 < t < 6$, at which particle $P$ changes direction. Justify your answer.

rubric.point: $P$ changes direction at $t = 1$ and $t = 4$ because $v_P$ changes sign at each
accept: from positive to negative at $t = 1$, from negative to positive at $t = 4$
"$v_P = 0$" without the sign change does not earn the point

parts.sample: $v_P(t) = 6(t - 1)(t - 4)$ is 0 at $t = 1$ and $t = 4$. It changes from positive to negative at $t = 1$ and from negative to positive at $t = 4$, so particle $P$ changes direction at $t = 1$ and at $t = 4$.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Find the velocity $v_Q(t)$ of particle $Q$. At time $t = 3$, are particles $P$ and $Q$ moving in the same direction? Justify your answer.

rubric.point: $v_Q(t) = e^{-t/2} - \frac{t - 2}{2}e^{-t/2}$, by the product and chain rules

accept: the sign of $v_Q(3)$ with supporting work
$P$ moves left and $Q$ moves right at $t = 3$

parts.sample: By the product rule and the chain rule, $v_Q(t) = 1 \cdot e^{-t/2} + (t - 2) \cdot \left(-\frac{1}{2}e^{-t/2}\right) = \frac{4 - t}{2}e^{-t/2}$. Then $v_Q(3) = \frac{1}{2}e^{-3/2} > 0$, so $Q$ moves right. Also $v_P(3) = 6(2)(-1) = -12 < 0$, so $P$ moves left. They are moving in opposite directions at $t = 3$.
